record_type_quote: Study 1 is a direct replication of the original whereas Study 2 used a shorter list of stimuli to examine the potential effect of the diﬃculty of the probe digit task.

targets.authors: Waugh, N. C., & Norman, D. A.
targets.title: Primary memory.
targets.evidence_quote: The purpose of this replication is to verify the results obtained by Waugh and Norman (1965) because their participants do not constitute a statistically representative sample due to its lack of size and diversity (Faber & Fonseca, 2014).
targets.outcome_quote: Both studies’ results partially support Waugh & Norman’s claim, as participants were more likely to recall a digit that was followed by fewer interfering items.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit verdict over both studies states partial support; interference agrees while presentation-rate differences qualify the original claim.

reasoning: Two new participant studies re-test the one Waugh and Norman paper. Altmann and Schunn motivate the extension but are not themselves a target. Full seven-page article, identity, authors, study boundaries and references verified.
